plan: Given my value of $25, I aim to bid slightly below my value to maximize profit while still having a chance to win. Assuming Betty and Charles bid close to their values, I will bid $24. This ensures a potential profit if I win, as I would pay the third-highest bid. If I bid too high, I risk overpaying relative to my value. If I bid too low, I risk losing the auction. I will not bid above my value to avoid a negative profit.

Given my value of $31, my goal is to bid just enough to win against the others while minimizing costs. Assuming other bidders have values randomly between $0 and $49, they might bid near their value. To win, I should bid slightly above average. I will bid $31, equaling my value, to ensure any profit is maximized by paying a lower third-highest bid. This balances winning chances while avoiding overbidding and ensures profit if I win.

Given my private value of $9, I should aim to bid below my value to ensure a profit if I win. Assuming others bid close to their values, bidding too high risks a loss. I will bid $6, expecting that if others bid higher, I lose nothing, and if I win, I gain $3, assuming the third-highest bid is lower. This strategy balances the risk of overbidding with the potential for profit.
